lexingCheck: Token streams are hand-derived (harness/vector_sources.py); check_vectors.py re-lexes every input with tslex.py and harness/crosscheck.js compares them with the TypeScript 6.0.3 parser and scanner.

vectors.description: Empty input: zero tokens, insufficient-tokens, no k-grams.
Three tokens, fewer than k=5.
Exactly k=5 tokens: one k-gram, partial window selects it.
Period-3 repetition: equal hashes in one window; the rightmost wins.
Comment/whitespace pair, plain layout.
Same tokens as ts-format-a: CRLF, a multi-line block comment, and a line comment ended by U+2028.
Rename pair, original names and literals.
Rename pair: other names, number and string quote style.
A ')' closing an if header allows a regular expression.
Any other ')' is followed by division.
A '/' inside a class and an escaped '/' do not end the regex.
Regex after return/typeof/void; a keyword after '.' is an ident and is followed by division.
vectors.inputText: function f(a) { return typeof /x/ === 'object' ? a.return / 2 : void /y/i; }

vectors.description: Postfix '!' keeps the division state; prefix '!' keeps the regex state.
vectors.inputText: const r = total! / count!; const ok = !/^a/.test(s);

vectors.description: Postfix ++ and -- are followed by division.
Nested template inside a substitution, and an object literal whose '}' does not end the substitution.
Templates accept any escape lexically (NotEscapeSequence), raw CRLF, and '$' not followed by '{'.
'>>' closing two type-argument lists is one token (ECMAScript longest match).
vectors.inputText: let m: Map<string, Array<number>> = new Map<string, Array<number>>();

vectors.description: Shift and comparison operators by longest match.
A hashbang at offset 0 is trivia up to the line terminator.
Annex B HTML-like comments are not recognized: plain punctuators.
No semicolons are inserted; 'a\n(b)' stays a call.
Decimal, hex, binary, octal, separators, leading and trailing dots, exponents.
BigInt literals in every radix, with separators.
Legacy octal ends before '.', so 07.5 is two numbers; 08.5 and 0779 are NonOctalDecimal literals.
Private names are one token including '#'.
'?.' is one token unless a decimal digit follows.
Identifiers with \u escapes keep their written text and are always ident, even when they spell 'if'.
U+2160 starts, U+00B7, U+0345 and U+200D continue, U+309B (ID_Start, not XID_Start) starts; U+00A0 is white space.
LS inside a string, PS ending a line comment, PS inside a string, lone CR as a line break.
TypeScript-only and contextual words are ident; ECMAScript and strict-mode reserved words are keyword.
vectors.inputText:
type T = keyof typeof x;
abstract class C implements I { declare readonly a: number; static async of() {} }

vectors.description: Reserved words after '.' or '?.' are ident.
Decorators: '@' is punctuation; the rest are ordinary tokens.
Escaped quote, \x and \u{} escapes, line continuation, \8 and \0 are all lexically valid.
In ts-tokens '<' is never JSX: a type assertion is punctuation; a regex may follow '>'.
A line terminator before the closing '/'.
A '/' inside an unclosed class does not end the regex.
Unterminated template-middle/tail: reported at its '}'.
End of input inside a substitution: reported at the template-head.
A raw LF ends nothing: unterminated string.
\x needs two hex digits.
Termination is decided before escapes are validated.
A numeric literal must not be followed by IdentifierStart.
Consecutive numeric separators.
BigInt suffix after a fraction.
Legacy octal cannot take the BigInt suffix.
'1.' followed by an identifier start.
Radix prefix without digits.
An escape for a digit cannot start an identifier.
Surrogate escapes are not combined; each is invalid.
Bad escape in a private name: reported at '#'.
U+2E2F is Pattern_Syntax, not ID_Continue.
U+180E is not white space (not Zs) and not an identifier character.
'#' not followed by an identifier start.
A hashbang is recognized only at offset 0.
A '\' not followed by 'u' outside literals.
Closer that does not match the innermost opener.
End of input: innermost unclosed opener.
Block comment without '*/'.
Ill-formed UTF-8 inside a string.
A leading BOM is rejected (shared rule OD-1).
NUL is rejected even inside a string (shared rule).
Semicolon style pair, with semicolons.
Semicolon style pair, without semicolons: exact differs, normalized (';' dropped) equals ts-semi-a.
vectors.inputText:
let a = 1
let b = a + 2
f(b)

vectors.description: '}' of an object literal or class expression: division.
'}' closing an arrow body ('{' right after '=>'): regex.
Documented departure D-10: after a function declaration's '}' the profile lexes division (ECMAScript: regex).
Documented departure D-10: after a class declaration's '}' the profile lexes division (ECMAScript: regex).
'++', '!' and '--' after a line terminator (also one inside a block comment) are prefix: regex follows.
'yield', 'await' and 'throw' are followed by a regex.
vectors.inputText:
function* g() { yield /a/; }
async function h() { await /b/; throw /c/; }

vectors.description: A NonOctalDecimal integer part takes no separators, but its fraction and exponent do.
Plain JavaScript (.js) under ts-tokens (stage 1 mapping).
vectors.inputText:
var r = a / b / c, s = /=/g;
if (r) /x/.exec(s);

vectors.description: Limitation: a self-closing element without text lexes as punctuation under ts-tokens and is not rejected.
JSX with a closing tag in a .js file under ts-tokens: ';' starts a regex that never closes.
Documented departure: 'await' as a script-code identifier is still a keyword, so '/ 2;' starts a regex.
A lone CR ends nothing: unterminated string.
'0_1': a separator may not follow a lone leading 0.
